t=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$t/dest"
for h in 00 01 02 03 04; do : > "$t/dest/demo-20260101-${h}0000-000000.tar.gz"; : > "$t/dest/demo-20260101-${h}0000-000000.tar.gz.sha256"; done
echo "--- rotate --keep 2 (deletes 3 oldest, keeps newest 2):"
bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/rc2sr1-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep 2
echo "--- remaining:"; ls "$t/dest" | grep '\.tar\.gz$'
echo "--- dry-run on 2 remaining with --keep=1 (equals-form):"
bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/rc2sr1-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest="$t/dest" --name=demo --keep=1 --dry-run
echo "--- verify --help exit code:"; bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/rc2sr1-d/verify.sh --help >/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
rm -rf "$t"
tool_input.description: Manually exercise rotate deletion order and refactored flag forms

result:
The leftover scratch script in `/tmp` is outside the sandbox's auto-allowed paths; it's harmless and I left it rather than prompt for approval.

All 9 tests pass (`bash tests/run_tests.sh` → `all tests passed`), and a manual check confirms rotate now deletes the 3 oldest of 5 archives with `--keep 2` and nothing when the count equals `--keep`.

What was done:

- **`rotate.sh`** — bug 1: `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on an oldest-first sorted list, which deleted from the keep-th entry through the *newest* (with exactly N archives it deleted exactly the newest). Now surplus is the first `total - keep` lines (`head -n`), with the early-exit widened to `-le` so the zero-surplus case exits cleanly (macOS `head -n 0` is an error). The parser/`resolve_dir` block was replaced by a source of `lib/common.sh`; flags unchanged (verified `--help`, `=`-forms, `--dry-run`).
- **`verify.sh`** — bug 2: the archive name was parsed out of the sidecar's content by splitting on whitespace, truncating `my backup-…` to `backup-…` → "archive missing" → BAD/rc=2. The name is now taken from the sidecar's own filename minus `.sha256` (per DESIGN.md), and the digest comparison was switched from the unquoted `[ $expected == $actual ]` to `[[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]`. Also sources `lib/common.sh`.
- **`lib/common.sh`** — new: the shared option-parsing block and `resolve_dir`, with a double-source guard in the style of `lib/log.sh`; consumes the sourcing script's arguments so `usage`/`parse_local_option`/`die` must be defined first.
- **`tests/run_tests.sh`** — added a rotate section (2 checks: nothing deleted at exactly N; newest survives) and a verify regression test (archive named `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` verifies `ok` with rc=0).

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`; new file: `lib/common.sh`.
